l6.heading: L6 — Protocol Forensics
l6.subheading: One methodological choice, two rankings. The same predictions, scored under both mask-pairing modes.
l6.standing_note: These predictions are reconstructed to reproduce the duplicate-mask behaviour the ECCV 2024 correction documents. No checkpoint was run and no model produced them. This lab demonstrates the mechanism of the correction; it is not a reproduction of the published table.
l6.moved_legend: A highlighted row changed position between the two rankings. One methodological choice, and the order is not the same.
l6.published_note: These are figures on the full PSG test set, reported by the ECCV 2024 mask-pairing correction. This lab scores a four-pixel fixture. The two are not comparable and are not placed in one table.
l4.heading: L4 — Method Comparator
l4.subheading: One frame, one ground truth, several methods. Two-stage, one-stage and the VLM pipeline answer the same question in different ways, and the provenance chip says which kind each column is.
l4.no_columns: No predictions are committed for this frame yet, so there is nothing to compare. Plan 03 Task 4 produces them.
l4.latency_unmeasured: Latency has not been measured on this machine.
l3.heading: L3 — Long-Tail Lab
l3.subheading: The frequency baseline that humiliated the field, fitted and scored live in the browser.
l3.lambda: Blend λ (0 = prior only, 1 = visual only)
l3.zipf: Zipf exponent of the predicate distribution
l3.freq_caption: Fitted on class co-occurrence alone. It consults no pixels: there is no parameter through which an image could reach it, and it still posts a competitive R.
l3.visual_heading: A visual model that reads the tail
l3.visual_caption: Scores the rare relations correctly and the common ones poorly. Lower R, higher mR — which is the trade the field spent years failing to notice.
l3.identity: The identity that explains the gap (E6)
l3.identity_note: Recall and mean recall average the same per-predicate recalls under different weights. Nothing else differs, so the whole bias problem is the sign of one covariance. Flatten the Zipf exponent and it goes to zero.
l7.heading: L7 — Caption to Graph
l7.subheading: A sentence and a scene graph carry the same structure: nouns are nodes, and what sits between two nouns is an edge.
l7.caption: Caption
l7.placeholder: the person is holding a box on the table
l7.idle: Type a caption. The graph appears as you type; nothing here is behind a button.
l7.oov_cost: outside P. The error is counted twice: the illegal triplet occupies a rank a legal one could have held, and the relation it describes is left unmatched. One mistake, two costs.
l7.warn_no_predicate: Two nouns with no relation named between them, so no edge was drawn.
l7.warn_self_loop: A relation from a node to itself was dropped: a scene graph has no self-loops.
l7.warn_unparsed: A word in neither vocabulary was read as part of a predicate rather than as a node.
l8.heading: L8 — mini-ISG Annotator
l8.subheading: A model drafted these triplets. Correcting them is the work, and the number beside it is what that work costs.
l8.draft_note: What the model returned for this frame. It stays here so the before and the after are both on screen.
l8.reference_note: The corrected set committed with this project. It is one annotator's reading of this frame, made in one session, and it is not a key: where you disagree, look at the frame again rather than at this list.
l8.projection: {n} corrections on one frame. At this rate the authors' {images}-image set would take {total}. That is arithmetic and not a measurement: it assumes every frame is as much work as this one, and the frames are not alike.
